Breakdown: suggest --project 3,014ms (32.7%), coord touch + coord interrupts 2,167ms (23.5%), zpc inject 1,964ms (21.3%), manna context 810ms (8.8%), five python3 -c JSON parsers 724ms (7.9%), bootstrap --recommend 428ms (4.6%), all remaining shell 89ms (1.0%). (1) DELETE the suggest block (append_project_tooling, hooks/claude/agent-do-session-start.sh ~:208-250). (2) Replace the five 'python3 -c' JSON parsers with jq (~150-190ms each, jq does the same in ~10ms; the hook already depends on jq). ~650ms.
(3) Collapse 'coord touch' and 'coord interrupts' into one spawn (~1.1s each; one combined read halves it).

title: zpc: lesson identity + retract verb — memory that can change its mind
description: WHAT: give lesson/decision rows stable ids; add 'zpc retract <id> --evidence' (append-only tombstone row, refusal without evidence per the flip pattern, exit 2); inject filters retracted lessons and injects load-bearing retractions in their place; harvest re-derives patterns from the living corpus so consolidated wrongness washes out; retract surfaces the blast radius (all co-referring lessons/decisions/patterns by tag+term) for review. WHY: injection is now automatic, so a wrong lesson is automated anchoring — the dm-ck case: 'computation kernel' believed 18 months, falsifiable only when asked the right way. STATE: gated behind mn-3fcc56 (same file ownership).

title: zpc: exposure-ranked re-litigation — counsel audits the most-injected lessons
description: WHAT: rank lessons by exposure (inject frequency from access-log) x age x kind (world-state rots, technique mostly doesn't); periodically build receipts-only briefs from CURRENT code/reality and have counsel re-try the top-N under subtraction-shaped questions ('what breaks if this claim is removed / was it ever true'); divergence files a retract candidate for ratification. WHY: wrong lessons don't announce themselves — they are falsifiable only when asked the right way, so the asking must be mechanical. STATE: gated behind lesson-identity issue and mn-3fcc56.

title: zpc: anti-dogma delivery — memory injected as claims, never law
description: WHAT: (1) inject renders every lesson/pattern WITH its epistemic status: date learned, kind (world-state|technique), last-verified, challenge count — no bare assertions; (2) the protocol header inverts authority: replace 'Established Patterns (follow these)' with the tie-breaker rule — recorded claims verified as of their date; live observation OUTRANKS memory; a contradiction between code and lesson is a finding to file, not a dissonance to rationalize; (3) cheap doubt: 'zpc retract --candidate <id> --evidence <receipt>' files a challenge without needing to win the argument (flag on existing verb, no taxonomy gate); challenged lessons jump the re-litigation queue and carry their challenge marker in inject. WHY: retraction assumes a noticer; injection suppresses noticing — dogma is beaten by falsifiable delivery plus cheap recorded doubt, not by hoping agents argue with their own birth context. STATE: gated behind mn-3fcc56 (file ownership) and mn-96f2e1 (needs lesson ids).

title: zpc security: confine counsel log collector to the project root
description: WHAT: _counsel_latest_log (lib/counsel.sh:97) follows tmp/logs/latest via readlink and reads the resolved session dir and log file unconfined — an absolute or dot-dot symlink target (committable in git) reaches arbitrary local files, whose tail then lands in a counsel brief on disk and in a model call. Auto-relit + hook inject make this triggerable by merely opening a session in a hostile repo. FIX: realpath -e both the resolved session dir AND the final log path; require both under realpath of the project root; otherwise emit the declarative unavailable line. Regression test: symlink escape attempt yields the unavailable receipt, never file content. SOURCE: automated security review 2026-07-27, MEDIUM, severity raised by the automation chain.

title: zpc: mine past corrections into preference lessons
description: WHAT: zpc harvest --corrections — scan session transcripts (agent-do sessions FTS) for user-correction moments (too wordy / not what I asked / try again / interrupts), extract pair (what the assistant did -> what Erik said), write dated preference lessons with verbatim quote receipts to the user-global zpc layer, tagged preference,mined, dedup by content-hash id. Inject's global slice then delivers them to every session; challenge/retract machinery applies. Flags only, no new verbs. WHY: don't classify intent forward, mine misses backward — receipts over guesses.

title: hooks: one-keystroke correction channel (w/d/s)
description: WHAT: UserPromptSubmit hook matching EXACT single-key prompts — w (too wordy: re-answer kernel-first), d (go deeper on the last answer), s (re-answer via subtraction form). Expands the key into explicit correction context for the model AND appends a receipt {ts,key,cwd} to ~/.agent-do/zpc/corrections.jsonl. Exact-match command vocabulary, not prose guessing. Kill switch AGENT_DO_CORRECTION_KEYS=0. Registered via install.sh spec list. WHY: correction must cost one keystroke; each press is intent data with a receipt.

title: CLAUDE.md: kernel-first reply contract (expansion on pull)
description: WHAT: one law in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Say the Thing section: default reply = answer in ~5 lines + load-bearing specifics; detail only on pull. Structure beats style instructions because instructions lose to session momentum. Executed directly by orchestrator.

title: zpc: inject --preferences — global slice with no store required
description: WHAT: flag on inject rendering ONLY the user-global slice (preference+technique lessons, patterns-free), <=2000 chars with the standard truncation marker, works when NO .zpc store exists (skip ensure_zpc; empty output + exit 0 when global file absent). No new verbs. WHY: Erik directive 2026-07-28: global preferences follow me everywhere.

title: hooks: auto-init .zpc in git repos + inject preferences everywhere
description: WHAT: (1) SessionStart (claude + codex) auto-runs zpc init when cwd is inside a git repo with no .zpc up-tree; silent, bounded 3s, kill switch AGENT_DO_ZPC_AUTOINIT=0. (2) When no store/records exist, hook embeds 'zpc inject --preferences' output so global preferences reach every session anywhere. WHY: Erik directive 2026-07-28: every project gets a store by default; preferences are user-level, not project-level.

title: zpc: init --store-only — a store without the repo edits
description:
WHAT: add --store-only to 'zpc init'. Creates .zpc/{memory,team,.state} + data files and updates the global project index; SKIPS the .gitignore append (integration.sh:522-529) and the instruction-file write/append (integration.sh:555-573). Keep init's leak protection without touching a tracked file by writing '.zpc/' into .git/info/exclude when the repo does not already ignore it. Must appear in cmd_init's --help usage line: the hooks gate on that string.

WHY: mn-1fb38d auto-runs init at every SessionStart in every git worktree. Plain init is not store-only — verified 2026-07-28 in a scratch repo: after 'agent-do zpc init', .gitignore gained the .zpc/ block and a pre-existing AGENTS.md gained a trailing '@.zpc/zpc-brain.md' line. A silent session-start hook may not edit tracked files in a repo it does not own, least of all an agent instruction file.

STATE: hooks/claude/agent-do-session-start.sh and hooks/codex/agent-do-session-start.py (commit 801268d) already implement auto-init and gate it POSITIVELY on the literal string '--store-only' appearing in 'zpc init --help'. init's arg loop swallows unknown flags (integration.sh:485), so an ungated call would silently run the invasive path. Until this ships the gate stays shut: no auto-init, no repo mutation, and the preferences half of mn-1fb38d is unaffected and already live. Shipping this flag turns auto-init on with no further hook change.

title: hooks: session memory is cwd-scoped — a subdir session misses its own project's store
description:
WHAT: both SessionStart hooks resolve the store as literally $CWD/.zpc (hooks/claude/agent-do-session-start.sh append_zpc_memory, hooks/codex/agent-do-session-start.py zpc()). zpc itself resolves a store by walking UP from cwd (tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh:resolve_zpc_dir). So a session started in a subdirectory of a repo whose store lives at the toplevel does not see that store at all.

RECEIPT (2026-07-28, real dispatcher): scratch repo with 1 recorded lesson at toplevel; hook run with cwd=<repo>/src/deep emitted the global ZPC Preferences slice, not the project's memory and not the advisory. Same result on both hooks.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: not a regression — before mn-1fb38d a subdir session got no ZPC section whatsoever, so preferences are strictly an improvement. But auto-init (mn-1fb38d + mn-39a482) means stores now exist in every git repo, which makes cwd-scoping the thing standing between a subdir session and memory that demonstrably exists two directories up. Monorepo and package-subdir sessions are the common case.

FIX SHAPE: resolve the store root by walking cwd up to the git toplevel (auto-init already does exactly this walk), then feed that root to the records check and to inject's cwd instead of $CWD. Constraint: the record-bearing path must stay byte-identical for sessions started AT the store root — that equivalence is pinned by mn-1fb38d's verification and is the regression guard for this change (run the orig-vs-new context diff on a repo with records).

NOT CLAIMED BY LANE 22: out of that lane's pinned contract; filed rather than folded in, because it changes store resolution on the exact path mn-1fb38d had to keep byte-stable.

title: zpc: bound resolve_zpc_dir's upward walk (toplevel, HOME floor, ownership)
description: WHAT: tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh resolve_zpc_dir walks up unbounded, same class as the hook finding (mn-90eb96 security rider): from a scratch cwd it can adopt a planted /tmp/.zpc or another user's store as the project store — every zpc command would then read AND write attacker-controlled memory. FIX: stop at git toplevel when inside a worktree; never ascend past $HOME (probe $HOME last); outside $HOME with no worktree, probe cwd only; trust only stores owned by the current uid (stat -f %u on darwin). Regression: planted-store matrix + existing store resolution unchanged. SOURCE: automated security review 2026-07-28, MEDIUM.

title: SECURITY: hook store walk was unbounded — planted store could inject trusted memory
description:
SEVERITY: local prompt injection + write into an attacker-controlled directory. Introduced by 051bb1e (mn-90eb96), fixed by 6245645. Never shipped in a release; window was within one session.

VULNERABILITY: both SessionStart hooks resolved a zpc store by walking cwd upward with no ceiling and no ownership check. A session opened anywhere under a world-writable directory (macOS /tmp is sticky but world-writable) would discover a .zpc planted above it and embed its lessons under the heading 'This project's recorded memory. Read it before coding' — attacker-controlled text in the trusted region of the agent's context, unattended, at session start. The same resolution chose the write-nudge baseline's location, so the hook also wrote into that directory.

REPRODUCED 2026-07-28 before fixing: store planted at /tmp/<dir>/.zpc with a lesson whose takeaway was a marker string; session cwd two levels below; marker appeared in additionalContext under the ZPC Project Memory heading on the claude hook. Confirmed zero after the fix on both hooks.

FIX (6245645): (1) ceiling — a git worktree stops at its toplevel, a cwd under $HOME stops at $HOME, a cwd outside both probes only itself; a worktree rooted above $HOME does not lift the $HOME ceiling. (2) ownership — a discovered store is used only when st_uid == getuid(), following symlinks (stat -L / Path.stat) so a .zpc symlinked elsewhere is judged by what it resolves to. A store not owned by the current uid ends the walk rather than being climbed past.

TESTS: tests/test_hook_store_resolution.py covers planted-store-not-discovered (with and without a worktree below it), the $HOME ceiling, and unowned-store-refused on both hooks with the uid spoofed, since an unprivileged test cannot chown. In-boundary behavior unchanged: deep subdirectory still reaches its own project memory; session at the store root byte-identical to pre-lane.

NOTE FOR THE ZPC SURFACE: zpc's own resolve_zpc_dir (tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh) is still an unbounded, ownership-blind walk. That is lower risk because it runs when a human invokes it rather than silently at session start, but 'agent-do zpc inject' run by hand from /tmp has the same exposure. Worth a decision by the zpc owner: bound it, or document that it trusts cwd's ancestry.

title: DREAM: agent-be as a second face on agent-do
description: Split the vocabulary without splitting the repo: an agent-be entry point (symlink, argv0-aware dispatch) exposing only the identity domain, with 'domain: be' tags in the one registry on zpc/context/sessions; manna and coord deliberately unclassified until usage shows which face reaches for them. Do-tools touch the world (browse, db, render, slack); be-tools are memory and judgment. Erik 2026-07-28: 'agent-do should feel pure (interacting with the world via structured discipline).' Orchestrator recommendation was yes-minimal; Erik parked it. Falsifier if built: nothing invokes agent-be within a month (receipts) = vanity alias, drop it. Reopen trigger: agent-do gets real public distribution, which forces the question anyway. DECIDE LATER — no agent executes this.

title: install.sh: warn when an installed wrapper has no settings registration
description: WHAT: install.sh installs hook wrappers unconditionally (step 4) but only merges settings.json when --register-hooks / interactive-yes. A run without the flag therefore leaves wrappers on disk for hooks that never fire, silently — this happened live 2026-07-28: correction-keys wrapper installed 13:19, never registered, w/d/s dead with no signal. FIX: at the end of a run, compare installed wrapper names against the registered set in settings.json and print a loud line naming each dead wrapper plus the exact re-run command. Read-only check, no auto-write. SOURCE: orchestrator verification 2026-07-28.

title: manna: dreams are inert until Erik converts them
description: WHAT: (1) 'claim' refuses type:dream with exit 2 and a message pointing at conversion (no status change, nothing written); (2) dreams STAY VISIBLE everywhere they are today — list, context, status — Erik's ruling 2026-07-28: 'I don't want them hidden from work lists, I want them visible and denied without conversion'; visibility is the point, the refusal is the gate; (3) render dreams with an unmistakable inert marker in list/context output (e.g. [DREAM: not claimable — requires Erik's conversion]) so an agent reading the board sees both the idea and its status as un-actionable; (4) conversion 'update <id> --type item' is the authorization act and prints an explicit line saying the dream is now claimable work; (5) 'show' unchanged. WHY: verified 2026-07-28 that dream is convention only — orchestrator claimed a dream successfully and dreams appear in both list and the agent context blob, so an agent scanning the board can build one unasked. Rust tool: cargo build --release + cargo test.

title: DREAM: agent-handoff — successor briefing assembled from live state
description: Chris's idea 2026-07-28, working name agent-handoff. The ritual he does by hand: paste end-of-session chats + state-of-things into a new orchestrator ('you are a new project agent... review manna, review handoffs, review intent, tell me where we are and where we're headed'). Two halves: ASSEMBLY (build the successor brief) and CAPTURE (per-session narrative). Orchestrator's read: assembly needs NO new storage for v1 — manna context + coord status/history + zpc inject/patterns + git log since last handoff + agent-sessions summaries already contain the state of things; the brief is a bounded render of those, plus the reader preamble. Capture (session-end journal entry, the narrative arc zpc deliberately doesn't keep) is the real new object and belongs on the SessionEnd hook. TAXONOMY GATE: whether this is a new tool or verbs on an existing domain (sessions/zpc) is Erik's ruling; do not build either way until converted. DECIDE LATER.

title: git: worktree add binds memory and board to the primary checkout
description: WHAT: 'agent-git worktree add' currently seeds ignored files (.env, .env.*, CLAUDE.local.md, .agent-do/worktree-seed) but leaves two silent traps: (1) .zpc/ is gitignored (.gitignore:36) so a fresh worktree has NO store, and the SessionStart auto-init shipped 2026-07-28 creates an empty one at the worktree toplevel — every lesson that lane writes dies when the worktree is removed; (2) manna resolves .manna relative to the checkout (tools/agent-manna/src/store.rs:17) with no path override, so each worktree carries its own copy of the tracked board and parallel claims diverge. FIX: on worktree add, bind the new tree's .zpc to the primary store (symlink or pointer honored by resolve_zpc_dir) and either point manna at the primary board or refuse with a message naming the divergence. Both must survive worktree removal without data loss. Verify: lesson written from inside a worktree is present in the primary store after 'worktree remove'; a claim made from a worktree is visible to the primary checkout. WHY: worktree isolation silently breaks the memory and coordination layers built 2026-07-27/28.

title: coord: name the remedy when contention means isolation
description: WHAT: coord already raises a contention interrupt when two writers claim overlapping paths (agent-coord v2 roles/territories). Extend the interrupt text to name the remedy explicitly — 'agent-do git worktree add <branch>' — and add the second trigger it cannot see today: a lane whose declared branch differs from the parent checkout's HEAD (one working tree holds one branch, so that case is mandatory isolation, not a preference). Nudge only, never block: same ladder as the enforcement trinity. Kill switch consistent with existing coord env conventions. WHY: whether to isolate should not depend on an agent's taste; coord holds the ownership truth, so it should say the remedy out loud. Orchestrator position stated 2026-08-03: ownership beats isolation for same-branch parallel work; evidence is the 2026-07-27/28 memory-OS build (12 lanes, one tree, zero clobbering).

title: docs: lane template states the isolation rule
description: WHAT: docs/LANE-PROMPT-TEMPLATE.md gains one line under the claim block: isolation is required when your branch differs from the parent checkout's HEAD or when your owned paths overlap another live lane's; otherwise stay in the shared tree and own your paths. Cite 'agent-do git worktree add' as the mechanism and the memory/board binding caveat (mn-68d471) so no lane invents its own workaround. Small docs edit; no code. WHY: the rule must reach the agents who read prompts, not only the orchestrator.

title: zpc write-nudge misreads a bound worktree
description: The Stop hook hooks/claude/agent-do-zpc-write-nudge.sh resolves the store cwd-only ([ -d .zpc ] at line 61, STATE_DIR at :64, zpc_line_count glob at :80). In a worktree bound by 'agent-git worktree add' (mn-68d471) that .zpc is a pointer directory: the hook counts 0 memory lines forever and writes its baseline into the stub, so from the second Stop on it nudges 'you changed code and wrote no memory' even when every lesson landed in the primary store. Not lossy, just wrong. FIX: follow the pointer for STATE_DIR and zpc_line_count only, keeping cwd for the git change detection (the code moved in the worktree, the memory lives in the primary) — same trust rules as tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh:_zpc_store_pointer_target. The position-nudge hook shares the cwd-only check but only tests existence, so it is unaffected.

title: zpc security: memory bindings live in AGENT_DO_HOME, not in the repo
description: WHAT: the worktree memory binding (80cff36) is a repo-resident pointer at .zpc/primary-store, honored by _zpc_store_pointer_target (tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh:9, resolution below). .zpc/ is gitignored so the pointer is normally untracked, but a repository can force-add one, and cloning that repo silently redirects where every session reads AND writes memory (uid check limits targets to stores this user owns — including other projects' stores — so cross-project context injection and misdirected writes are both reachable with zero user action, since session-start injection is automatic). Repository content must never carry authority over where memory lives. FIX (preferred): keep bindings in a user-owned registry under $AGENT_DO_HOME keyed by absolute worktree path, written by 'agent-git worktree add', resolved by zpc; repo-resident pointers stop being honored. MINIMUM: refuse any pointer that git tracks (git ls-files --error-unmatch) AND require a matching registry entry. Keep the existing uid/ownership checks and the bounded walk; planted-store regressions must still pass. SOURCE: automated security review 2026-08-03, MEDIUM.

title: zpc security: a tracked .zpc store injects a repo's own text as project memory
description: ADJACENT to mn-84b9dc, found while closing it, NOT introduced by it. .zpc/ is gitignored in this repo but nothing stops any other repository from tracking .zpc/memory/lessons.jsonl. On clone it is a directory the cloning user owns, so the store walk accepts it and the session-start hook injects its contents under a heading that tells the agent this is the project's recorded truth (hooks/claude/agent-do-session-start.sh, append_zpc_memory). Repo content still becomes agent instructions; mn-84b9dc only closed the redirection half (a repo can no longer point at ANOTHER store). SCOPE: this is a design decision, not a bug fix — tests/test_worktree_binding.py::test_binding_is_bounded currently asserts a tracked store IS respected, on the reading that memory travelling with a branch is legitimate. Options: (a) keep, documented; (b) refuse stores git tracks (git ls-files --error-unmatch), which breaks the deliberate tracked-store case; (c) accept tracked stores but mark injected content as untrusted in the hook's heading. Erik picks.

title: hooks: stamp now on every turn (the temporal anchor)
description: WHAT: UserPromptSubmit hook injects one line per turn: absolute ISO local timestamp + weekday, elapsed since previous turn, elapsed since session start. Bounded (~1 line, <=120 chars), silent exit 0 on any failure, kill switch AGENT_DO_NOW=0, registered via install.sh CLAUDE_SETTINGS_SPECS + uninstall list; codex parity if its prompt hook supports injection. WHY: a model gets one clock reading at session start and then does date arithmetic against stale context — verified failure 2026-08-03: this orchestrator wrote '2026-07-28' into issues and lane prompts it created ON 2026-08-03, six days off, while proposing this very fix. Per-turn stamps also leave a trail of real 'now' moments in the transcript, so references to previous moments become readable instead of guessed.

title: zpc+manna: dated records render their age, so nobody does the arithmetic
description: WHAT: everywhere the system injects or lists dated records, render the age beside the date: '2026-07-27 (7d ago)'. Surfaces: zpc inject (lessons, patterns, corrections, preferences slice), zpc position/counsel output, manna list/show/context. Rendering happens at output time from the stored ISO timestamp; stored data is unchanged. WHY: models copy phrases reliably and compute date deltas unreliably. Existing proof: agent-coord already renders 'last_seen 3m ago' and its ages are never misreported, unlike bare-date records. Bound: age strings must not push inject past its existing char bounds.

title: DREAM: a time surface for on-demand truth (now/since/render)
description: Third piece of the 2026-08-03 temporal design, parked because it is a taxonomy ruling only Erik makes: whether 'now', 'since <ts>', 'render <ts>' (returns the correct English phrase for a delta) live as a new tool or as verbs on an existing domain. Pieces 1 and 2 (per-turn stamp mn-2895c2, pre-rendered ages mn-1da238) cover recorded records and the live conversation; this covers the residual case where an agent must produce a relative phrase for something not already rendered, and should ask instead of inventing. Honest limit of the whole design, worth restating here: it makes references to RECORDED events correct; it cannot fix a vague 'we discussed this recently' about something never recorded, except insofar as the per-turn stamp covers the conversation itself. DECIDE LATER — no agent executes this.

title: zpc: derive the memory bounds — a made-up number is deleting 197 of 197 lessons
description: RECEIPT (measured 2026-08-03): SessionStart against /Users/erik/Custom-Coding/palingenesis delivers 6303 chars of ZPC memory containing protocol + profile + partial patterns and ZERO of the store's 197 lessons; the entire loss is reported as the literal '[zpc inject truncated]' with no magnitude. Cause: the 6000-char hook bound (hooks/claude/agent-do-session-start.sh append_zpc_memory, mirrored in the codex hook), plus inject's own internal top-N which already drops 197 to 30 before the hook cuts again. Neither number was derived; the orchestrator picked them 2026-07-27. WHAT: (1) replace every invented bound in the zpc delivery path with a value derived from a real constraint or remove it — the operative constraints are the session context window (a 6000-char blob is ~0.7% of a 200k-token context) and the hook's own 3s/10s time budget, which is a TIME bound not a SIZE bound; (2) rank-then-fit rather than truncate mid-stream, so a bound cuts the least valuable records instead of whatever lands past a byte offset; (3) every truncation marker must carry magnitude and totals: '[truncated: 30 of 197 lessons, 12 of 44 decisions]' — the fact of a cut without its size is a half-receipt; (4) same treatment for --compact (2000), mining (20 of 76 candidates), re-litigation (top 3), harvest staleness (7d/5 lessons): derive, or declare the constraint that forced the number. WHY: this is the arbitrary-cap disease in the system whose sole job is to prevent silent knowledge loss. Erik 2026-08-03: 'I DO NOT want AI to ever arbitrarily cap stuff.'

title: quantities: the authority — real ceilings and measured totals, one source of truth
description: WHAT: generalize models.yaml's capability records into a quantity authority every consumer reads instead of typing a literal, plus a read surface to query it. Two kinds of quantity: LOOKED-UP (model max_tokens/max_input_tokens/context windows, API page ceilings, rate limits — static, versioned, already partly present at models.yaml:43) and MEASURED (how many rows/files/records/results exist right now — a census). Read surface as VERBS on an existing domain (default: harness), NOT a new tool: the taxonomy gate is Erik's ruling and this lane does not open it. WHY: agents guess numbers because measuring costs a tool call and guessing costs nothing; make measurement cheaper than invention and the motive dies. This is the authority layer of the quantity-contracts stack; the gate (mn-TBD) and the write-time check (mn-TBD) both read it.

title: quantities: the gate — bounds declared, drift caught, totals audited
description: WHAT: make an unreceipted quantity fail the build, using the machinery that already holds 95 tools honest. Four parts mirroring the contracts layer: (1) DECLARATION — every registry command that bounds output or returns a collection declares its bound's provenance beside its contracts block: {source: registry|measured|derived|none, ref: <authority key or expression>, why: <the constraint>}; (2) GATE — 'harness contracts validate' fails any bounding command with no declaration, same run that already fails an undeclared contract, already wired into test.sh; (3) DRIFT — the highest-value new check: compare each declared bound against the authority and fail a bound that is a small unexplained fraction of the real ceiling (the case that would have caught inject at 6000 chars against a 200k-token context); (4) AUDIT — behavioral probe: run the command, verify output carries totals and that any truncation marker carries magnitude, not just the fact of a cut. Plus the outward form of drift: scan a project outside agent-do for bare numeric literals in bounding positions near LLM/DB/HTTP calls and report each against the known ceiling — inventory first, because the pollution is already shipped. WHY: Erik 2026-08-03, 'it must be enforced via agent-do'; a doc line fixes nothing (518 lessons, zero readers).

title: quantities: the write-time check — a bare literal never reaches a shipped file
description: WHAT: hook on Edit/Write that inspects new content for bare numeric literals in bounding positions (max_tokens, max_output_tokens, budget_tokens, thinking budgets, temperature/top_p where capped, top_k, LIMIT, page_size, batch_size, chunk_size, timeout, retries/max_retries, max_iterations, max_depth, slice/head/tail bounds) and checks them against the quantity authority. Nudge mode first, naming the real ceiling and the remediation hierarchy (omit the parameter > reference a capability constant > named constant carrying its derivation comment); block mode available once the false-positive rate is measured, same ladder as the enforcement trinity. Kill switch; silent exit 0 on every failure path; registered through install.sh (three places). WHY: this is the class Erik named primary — a cap the agent writes into project X runs on every request forever, looks like configuration so it survives review, and fails silently by truncating mid-response. The write moment is the only point where it is still cheap to fix.

title: quantities: the authority does not know the model it runs on (claude-opus-5 absent)
description: RECEIPT (measured 2026-08-04, after a0b5ff7): 'harness quantity lookup anthropic.claude-opus-5.max_tokens' exits 1, unknown key. 'harness quantity keys --prefix anthropic' lists opus-4-8, sonnet-5, haiku-4-5 and models_list.page_limit; grep for claude-opus-5 in models.yaml returns 0. So the authority built to stop agents inventing ceilings has no record for the current Opus model, which means a consumer asking for it correctly gets a refusal and the tempting fallback is exactly the literal the program forbids. WHAT: close the coverage gap and keep it closed — refresh the records ('models doctor' is the refresh path per CLAUDE.md), and add a coverage check so a model reachable through the router with no authority record is a loud failure rather than a silent unknown. The check belongs with the drift work (mn-741a02) if it fits there; decide and say which. WHY: an authority with holes teaches the workaround it exists to prevent.

title: suggest --project walks the whole tree to answer one yes/no
description: MEASURED 2026-08-10 by cProfile against /Users/erik/Custom-Coding/palingenesis: 'agent-do suggest --project' takes 10.5s, of which 7.6s is one line. bin/suggest:124 — 'if (project_root / "migrations").exists() or list(project_root.rglob("*.sql")):' — recursively walks the entire project to decide whether to add a database signal: 195,249 posix.scandir calls, pathlib _select_from 5.19s + scandir 3.54s. It descends node_modules, .venv, Rust target/, .git. Two defects in one line: the walk is unbounded (no prune list, no depth limit), and list() forces the complete enumeration when the answer is known at the first match. No AI is involved anywhere in this path — verified AGENT_DO_SUGGEST_AI=off 11.1s vs on 11.3s — so no model or setting is the cause. title: Manna: ordered handoff names — NN[bMM] prefix as a derived build product
description:
PURPOSE OF THE b-MARKER (Erik, 2026-08-20): a launch gate for parallel sessions. Any file without a b is safe to open in its own parallel session right now; a b means do not launch until the named blocker closes. The fence is per-file, not positional: 01 02 03 04b03 05 = four launchable (01, 02, 03, 05), only 04 held. Corollary filing rule: the number encodes PRIORITY ONLY, never dependency — every real dependency must be a blocked_by edge on the board, or a bare filename will wrongly read as launchable. The sync pass keeps markers live so absence-of-b is always a true launch signal.

DECIDED: A+B — two renderings of one board truth. Numbered filenames for the human glance; generated .handoff/README.md index (number ↔ mn-id ↔ full blocker list ↔ status) for agents and traceability. Both written by the same sync pass; agents read the board, never filenames.

DECIDED, ordering: no gap numbering, no insertion markers (5.inject rejected — records history where names should record current state). Order lives on the board as an ordered list; every sync re-derives dense 01..N and renames whatever moved. The tool owns every rename atomically; git history is the record of how the plan changed.

DECIDED, blocker suffix: exactly one b-marker — the highest still-open blocker. 05b02 even when 05 also waits on 01: 02's own name carries b01, so the chain reads through. Sync re-derives on every change — when the shown blocker closes but another remains, the name re-renders to it; when the last closes, the b vanishes (that bare name IS the launch signal). Edge case (independent blockers, only one shown) is covered by the README's full list.

THE SCHEME (proven by hand in vms.io .handoff/): filename = <NN>[b<MM>]-mn-<id>-<slug>.md. Two-digit priority prefix; a blocked item wears b + its highest still-open blocker's number. Payoff: ls .handoff/ reads as the plan — priority, blockage, and parallel-launch safety at a glance.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT: numbering is a derived build product the tool owns, never hand-maintained — contracts-propose doctrine. Hand-kept copies drift (vms.io's rename pass broke three times in one session). Mechanism: a sync pass (new verb, or reconcile --fix growing rename powers) computes prefixes from board state, renames files, repoints prompt: fields, and regenerates the README index atomically; manna lint flags filename-vs-board drift. Pairing gate already accepts prefixed names (canonical_handoff_path requires only .md under .handoff/); generation at workflow.rs:317 plus sync/lint logic are the changes.

REMAINING WORK, not decisions: ordered-list/rank storage on items, the sync pass, lint wiring. Design settled. Build waits for conversion (--type item) and a clear lane — codex session active when filed. New manna verb/field = taxonomy gate, satisfied by this thread.

title: Harness: browse interactive login forks the save away from the canonical session name
description:
Root cause of Erik's two-week double-login pattern (vms.io Strety capture 2026-08-21 was the fourth incident). Mechanism, verified in source: resolve_save_target_name (tools/agent-browse/agent-browse:86) silently forks a save to <name>@<agent-session> whenever the plain name already exists and the daemon is agent-scoped — so a fresh human MFA login saved with 'login done --save strety' lands at strety@tmux-22 while the expired canonical stays enthroned. session load (agent-browse:1290) is literal — no fork awareness — so every other lane loads the stale canonical, hits the sign-in wall, and asks the human to log in again. Repair attempts recurse: 'session save strety' forks right back unless --shared is passed, reporting success:true with the real name buried in JSON.

Fix, three parts: (1) 'login done --save' defaults to --shared — a human-completed interactive login is inherently the shared credential; fork-on-write protection is for automated saves, never for an MFA ceremony. (2) Any save that forks must surface a top-level warning naming the fork and the --shared escape — a silent redirect reporting success is the killer. (3) 'session load <plain>' should warn when a fresher agent-scoped fork exists (staleness beats name purity); consider a 'session promote <name>@<agent>' verb to bless a fork into canonical.

Canonical strety was repaired manually 2026-08-21 (load strety@tmux-22 → save strety --shared → live-navigation verified authenticated). Interim rule until this ships: every login-done save carries --shared.

(2) When the spark exceeds the title bound, the error must teach the split: 'a spark is a title — put the substance in --description'. 5. Migration/adoption: what happens to today's prose-linked pairs; does the sibling convention remain the recommended floor even if a feature ships.

VERIFY the codex hook surface against its live docs/config before choosing the mechanism — do not assume injection exists. (4) GUARDRAILS (doctrine, enforce in code where cheap): bells carry no payload (refuse a bell with content); workers may request contract changes via need but never self-amend acceptance criteria; a bell exchange is never a close — done still requires executed receipts. USE CASE that motivated it: a worker hits an easy-fix failure mid-claim, rings the orchestrator, they coordinate ON THE LEDGER (drops/needs), the item progresses under its original claim — replacing Erik hand-pasting failure reports between sessions. The no-reopen law is untouched: this serves LIVE claims only. Tests: ring lands at next turn boundary per harness; content-bearing bell refused; dead-session ring degrades silently; ledger entries remain the only substance. title: Harness: build agent-do superhuman for Split Inboxes, Auto Labels, and Auto Archive
description:
## Goal

Build `agent-do superhuman` to manage the persistent organization settings in Superhuman itself: Split Inboxes, Auto Labels, and Auto Archive rules. Erik wants substantial control over filters and inboxes. Message search or one-time bulk triage alone does not satisfy this item.

## Required behavior

- Account discovery and explicit account selection; doctor and snapshot distinguish documented capability, available capability, authenticated access, and verified readiness.
- Split Inboxes: list/show definitions, preview matching conversations, create/update, reorder, disable, hide when empty, and control whether matches also appear in Important/Other.
- Auto Labels: list/show, create/update deterministic conditions and AI prompts where the account supports them, AND/OR composition, exclusions, and product-native previews. Report plan limits and retrospective application honestly.
- Auto Archive: inspect and change label-based archiving, Always Archive, and Never Archive for senders/domains. Preserve Superhuman precedence and identify any provider-native rule interaction.
- Configuration plans show before/after changes, affected account and objects, and supported verification. Apply only against the expected current state, serialize mutations, read back after reload, and record receipts. Repeating a request must not create duplicates. A stale plan, wrong account, expired login, absent control, or failed prerequisite stops the write.
- Keep `agent-do email` as the general mailbox surface. Superhuman owns its rules and classification; do not create a competing local routing engine or substitute Gmail/Outlook rules for Superhuman settings.

## Transport and implementation

1. Discover the authenticated official MCP tool surface at https://mcp.mail.superhuman.com/mcp before freezing capability claims. The October 22 review found documented split/label reads and thread updates, but no documented configuration writes. Published examples are not an exhaustive live schema.
2. Use official supported operations where present. For required settings absent from the official interface, implement and test the actual Superhuman settings UI through existing `agent-do browse` or `agent-do macos`. Prove that path early. A chat connector alone is not a standalone CLI implementation.
3. Reuse `creds`, appropriate `auth` infrastructure, browser/session control, JSON output conventions, and existing verification patterns. Browser login state and MCP authorization are distinct. Never log credentials, cookies, or unnecessary message bodies. Do not edit private app storage, invent undocumented endpoints, or bypass a broken production path.
4. Suggested command families: doctor, accounts, snapshot, splits, autolabels, archive-rules, plan, apply, verify. Final names should follow current repository patterns. All mutations are account-scoped and carry read-back results.
5. Register the tool, help, routing/discovery metadata, readiness requirements, and complete five-beat contracts with correct destructive/sensitive/own-state attributes. Add focused tests, root runner coverage, and user documentation. Follow repository approval rules for any genuinely new dependency.

## Acceptance and validation

- Fixture/contract coverage proves account isolation, pagination/completeness reporting, capability differences, duplicate prevention, stale-plan rejection, expired-auth failure, partial-write reporting, split ordering, exclusions, and archive precedence.
- On an authorized account, demonstrate configuration inventory, native preview, a controlled change through the intended transport, reload/read-back, and restoration of the original configuration. Record exact scope and outcomes without exporting private mailbox content. Distinguish restoring configuration from reversing any labels already applied to historical mail.
- Verify the required settings families, not just email search and thread edits. A failed or unavailable settings transport is an explicit unfinished requirement; no connector-only completion claim.
- Run the new focused suite, relevant existing email/auth/browser checks, formatting/lint/type checks applicable to the touched code, `agent-do harness contracts validate` with zero warnings, contracts drift checks for the new tool, and the canonical root gate required by the repo.
- Close under the repository receipt/commit rule. If an acceptance step can only be performed by Erik, track that exact field check separately; report unverified product behavior accurately.

## Starting evidence and prerequisites

Review pin: c664a81c024fb9a46bc3957528f614679cb0a16c. `agent-do email` includes Graph and local Mail index coverage; the review shell had no configured Graph access. The existing email fixture suite and 32 Graph/coverage tests passed. There is no registered `agent-do mail` tool.

Superhuman is installed as /Applications/Superhuman.app (com.superhuman.electron), but AppleEvents probing found no scripting dictionary. The default Python lacked AppKit, built-in computer-use surfaces were disabled, and restored browser state reached only the public website. These are recorded review limitations, not proof of present failure; recheck live readiness before implementation. The official Superhuman plugin was available but uninstalled at review time. Business/Enterprise and Ask AI were documented MCP prerequisites; verify account eligibility and permissions rather than assuming access.

## Sources

- Full assessment: .dev/2026-10-22-superhuman-feasibility.md (also copied to iCloud Transfer and the Erkverse Obsidian vault). This work order carries the build requirements so it does not depend on an ignored local report.
- Official MCP: https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005696690317-Superhuman-Mail-MCP-Server
- Setup: https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/47980509830157-Set-Up-the-Superhuman-Mail-MCP
- Split Inboxes: https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005636204941-Custom-Split-Inbox
- Auto Labels: https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005657758861-Auto-Labels
- Auto Archive: https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005662460813-Auto-Archive

2. Closure assessment: one read-only structured CLI path explains target revision, integration evidence, outstanding required acceptance, authority and exact next action. Closure revalidates expected board/assignment/evidence state under locking and refuses stale assessment or incomplete acceptance. 3. Scoped coordinator authority: authenticated, explicit grant for bounded items/track scope, never self-elevated from an overseer label, pulse, claimed identity string, or shared worker secret. Coordinator can receive submission, request correction, accept and close, or release/cancel with reason. Submission is distinct from acceptance; remaining checks have a visible coordinator owner. Add a regression that registers with a transient anchor pid and asserts the peer is not dead while its pulse is fresh. title: Transferable leads and coordinated track teams: standalone authority and integration
description:
# Transferable project leads and coordinated track teams

Locked design: Erik's approved conversation plan, 2026-11-06. This filing authorizes work-order preparation, not implementation, worker launches, live notifications, publishing, deployment, or pilot activation. Canonical backlog and progress remain Manna; this document describes product invariants rather than a parallel ledger.

## Product and role
Any existing agent session can be designated lead for a project or track. No special agent type, new session requirement, fixed lifespan, or automatic context-quality scoring. A brainstorming session may become a lead when an idea becomes a workstream. Holy offers Make lead, Transfer lead, and Give this track its own lead. Designation alone launches no workers and starts no implementation.

One accountable lead per scope. An item resolves its track lead first and otherwise its project lead. Several scopes may have different leads, and one session may lead several scopes. A project lead may see track progress but may not silently override a track lead. No nested management hierarchy or lead elections in this build.

Agent-do is standalone and owns the durable designation: canonical project/board or track coordinate, exact session identity and proof binding, monotonically changed designation generation, explicitly granted authority, current brief pointers, and append-only appointment/transfer/authority history. Reuse the existing Manna/Coord/managed authority machinery rather than creating a second identity, backlog, credential store, or acceptance ledger. Choose the narrowest owning subsystem and extend its structured command contract; do not introduce an unrelated top-level tool. Holy is an adapter and UI, never the sole source of truth. The brief names objectives, current decisions, blockers and pending reviews by canonical IDs; it is not a copied progress ledger.

Role is distinct from authority. Authorities cover assignments, review/corrections, integration approval, final acceptance, named integration targets and separately granted publishing/PR/deployment operations. Appointment must not mint operator authority or bypass existing grants. Standing permissions avoid repeated questions within their scope. Every consequential operation verifies current scope, exact identity, generation, and authority, including after waiting for a lock and immediately before an external effect. Do not impersonate Erik. Launch authority is explicit and distinct from designation. Existing no-push/no-live-operation boundaries hold until authorized.

## Execution choices
Preserve Build item and Build track with one worker. Add Build track with a team. Single-worker tracks still claim children individually, obey required review, and do not monopolize child tickets. Team launch opens one session per actionable child ticket selected for that run, including currently blocked children: an eight-ticket track may open eight sessions while only three eligible workers begin. Decisions and dreams are not implementation workers. Completed items and tickets already owned elsewhere are displayed accurately, not relaunched.

Show the exact planned team and counts before launch (or operate under recorded standing launch authority). Record a stable launch/run identifier and each ticket-to-session assignment. Waiting is assignment, not an active Manna claim. Eligible workers re-read canonical state and claim before editing. Blocked sessions remain quiet, without model polling, token-spending loops, or asking Erik to relay messages. Manna decides order from dependencies and required gates; agents cannot negotiate around blockers through messages. Integration, review, acceptance and completion are distinct gates: a commit or submitted report never satisfies them by implication.

Repeated launch, concurrent hosts, partial launch, disconnect, crash, and retry must not create duplicate workers. A changed claim, work order, attempt, scope, lead or assignment invalidates stale operations appropriately. A manually launched worker that wins a ticket must be respected; never steal ownership. New tickets added after launch appear unassigned and need an explicit launch decision. Removed or moved tickets are reassessed, not blindly continued. A failed/closed worker becomes Needs replacement; no unbounded respawn. Replacement requires an explicit action or separately granted standing policy. Record uncertainty when a launch/delivery may have happened; reconcile evidence before retrying.

## Lead responsibilities and review
The lead translates requests into work orders, assigns workers, tracks progress, resolves questions, inspects submissions or commissions an independent reviewer, requests corrections, approves integration, accepts completed work and explains the project. It does not implement product code under the same role and then approve its own changes. Investigation, diff inspection, verification and integration are legitimate lead work; implementation corrections return to a worker. Approval records retain evidence of who reviewed what; review policy rejects author-as-independent-reviewer where independence is required.

Approval to integrate and final task acceptance are separate. Worker submits an exact revision and receipts; authorized lead approves that submission; MI prepares and validates an integration candidate; MI lands only while submission, claim incarnation, work-order binding, policy, target and approval remain valid; final acceptance checks any remaining installed/deployed/user-facing requirements. Existing repository policy must support checks-first as a preserved explicit option and review-and-checks as the orchestrated-team default. Do not silently activate MI or migrate an existing repository's policy.

An approval is bound to board/item, attempt, submission id, exact revision and the applicable work-order/policy evidence. Changed submissions invalidate it. Main advancing requires candidate rebuild and checks under the existing MI rules. Conflict resolutions or other introduced changes cannot silently inherit approval for different code: define and enforce exactly which resulting tree the approval covers. Revoked/expired or uncertain authority cannot authorize new effects. Recovery before landing revalidates the gate; recovery after landing completes the receipt without landing twice. Approval to integrate cannot be passed as final acceptance, and a trailer is never review approval.

## Transfer and continuity
Transfer changes the authoritative appointment and routes future questions/submissions to the new lead. Workers, branches and assignments stay put. The new lead gets the current brief plus canonical board, submission, approval, integration and blocker state, including honest unavailable-source status. The old lead loses authority for new decisions. Previously valid recorded approvals retain their original evidence and revision binding unless explicitly revoked or otherwise invalidated; transfer alone must not erase valid historical approvals. Test this distinction against in-flight actions, whose authority is rechecked before their consequential step. Completed effects remain completed. An outgoing lead need not be alive or cooperative; its final handoff is helpful but never required for transfer. Restarting Holy or replacing a conversation reconstructs state from agent-do.

## Wake delivery and UI
Use the existing coord-wake/1 contract, including durable dispatch-started before transport and unknown outcomes that prohibit blind retry. Holy uses its supported background inbox/readiness path, not GUI automation or unsolicited tmux input. Verify session incarnation and input readiness, preserve drafts and focus, queue while busy, and distinguish transport submission, prompt observation and worker acknowledgment. No delivery receipt grants approval or alters claims. Waiting workers wake only when their assignment and prerequisites are still current. Reuse mn-88d1ac, Holy mn-702ea1 and field check mn-aefa29; do not duplicate their work or treat their open live gate as passed.

Existing Holy surfaces gain a Lead badge, responsible lead on project/track views, assignment labels, scope/authority controls, and working/waiting/awaiting-review/needs-replacement/done team state. Waiting states name concrete prerequisite IDs and gates. Command-click remains selection, not launch. No new dashboard; do not flood the lead with every worker command. Remote/unavailable hosts remain explicit and never fall back silently to another board or host.

## Delivery order and acceptance
1. Agent-do durable scoped lead designation, transfer, authority, history, read model and recoverable state. Publish fixtures for Holy.
2. Agent-do pre-landing MI review gate and agent-do team assignment/eligibility lifecycle can proceed in parallel after the lead contract is accepted. Holy lead controls can proceed in parallel against that accepted contract.
3. Existing Holy wake support and its field check proceed independently. Holy team execution follows core assignments, lead controls, MI gate and wake implementation; installed acceptance requires the live wake gate.
4. Combined field check in one opted-in project: designate an existing lead, launch a team with ready and blocked items, verify quiet wait and automatic wake, reject/correct a submission, prevent old approval reuse, land under review policy, transfer lead mid-run without restarting workers, recover after Holy restart and partial launch, respect manual individual dispatch, and prove no duplicate launches or focus theft. Name source revisions, policy/authority, host/build and concrete receipts. Live checks require Erik's separately authorized project, sessions and build.

Cross-board depends_on relations currently express lineage, not an enforced block. Work orders must name exact cross-repo prerequisites and require their accepted contract/source evidence before dependent implementation and live effects. Local blocked_by edges enforce local order. Do not assume federation metadata alone enforces execution eligibility; runtime team behavior must use authoritative supported eligibility and fail closed on unavailable required evidence.

Each build returns SUBMITTED for independent review with exact commits, executed focused tests, sealed receipts and all remaining live gates. Keep field checks separate from source completion, preserve foreign dirt, commit only owned paths, and do not run board cleanup. No mandatory conversion of all existing items, new dependency/framework, automatic context scoring, elections, lead hierarchy, mandatory team execution, automatic publishing grant or hidden always-running model job. Existing single-worker track and MI pilot remain independently testable.
